matching: all clauses ANDed; scalar = equality, oneOf = membership, min/max inclusive

rules.name: FTP Brute Force Flow Pattern
rules.rationale: FTP control traffic commonly uses TCP port 21. Brute-force-like flows may show repeated short TCP connections with elevated packet rate. This is a flow-level heuristic and does not inspect FTP login payloads.

rules.name: SSH Brute Force Flow Pattern
rules.rationale: SSH control traffic commonly uses TCP port 22. SSH brute-force attempts often create repeated short TCP flows against SSH port 22. This is a flow-level heuristic and cannot inspect SSH authentication results.

rules.name: High Rate DoS Flow Pattern
rules.rationale: DoS-like flows may show high packet rate from one direction. Limited backward packet count can indicate poor response balance during a high-rate flow. This threshold is a prototype heuristic and should be calibrated with feature distribution analysis.

rules.name: Distributed High Rate Flow Pattern
rules.rationale: DDoS-like flows may show very high packet rate and strong forward traffic volume. Low backward packet count can indicate response imbalance under high-rate traffic. This is a single-flow heuristic and does not prove distributed source behavior by itself.

rules.name: Botnet Beacon-Like Flow Pattern
rules.rationale: Botnet communication can appear as longer-lived beacon-like flows. Moderate packet rate and forward packet count can indicate repeated command-and-control style communication. This heuristic does not use destination reputation or host history.

rules.name: Suspicious Web Flow Pattern
rules.rationale: Web attack traffic commonly uses HTTP or HTTPS destination ports. Larger packet length means can indicate request-heavy or payload-heavy web flows. This flow-level heuristic cannot inspect URLs, request parameters, SQL strings, or XSS payloads.

rules.name: Long Duration Infiltration-Like Flow Pattern
rules.rationale: Infiltration-like flows may involve longer duration network activity. Sustained bytes per second and backward packets can indicate interactive or data-transfer behavior. This heuristic is weak without host context, payload inspection, or post-compromise behavior analysis.
